items.label: f03-http-inside-row-lock
items.front: Outbox delivery holds FOR UPDATE row locks and an open transaction while making up to ten sequential HTTP calls. Risk and proposed shape?
items.back: A slow sink stretches lock and transaction time for the whole batch. Claim rows (mark and commit), send outside the transaction, then record the result — at the cost of a claim-expiry rule.

items.label: f01-ingest-admission-order
items.front: Signalpost ingest: in what order does the onRequest hook apply its gates, and when is the concurrency reservation released?
items.back: Concurrency cap first (429 Retry-After: 1), then authentication (401), then the Redis rate limit (429, or 503 on outage) — all before body parsing. The reservation (active++ plus the admitted WeakSet) is released in onResponse.

items.label: f04-readiness-gates
items.front: Name the three readiness gates in signalpost's assessment and the practical conclusion each one supports.
items.back: Foundation (U01-U06 behavior) -> ready for bounded independent feature practice. Independent delivery -> evidence relevant to mid-level responsibilities with supervision needs stated. Senior practice -> evidence to discuss with a practitioner; a solo course cannot establish a universal senior title.

items.label: f02-rollback-dead-connection
items.front: db.ts transaction helper: COMMIT fails because the connection died. What two things go wrong, and what is the fix?
items.back: The ROLLBACK can itself throw and replace the original error, and client.release() returns a dead client to the pool. Release with the error (client.release(error)) so the pool discards it.

items.prompt: Your API runs `SELECT ... WHERE email = $1` and inserts only when no row comes back. Why does U05 say this is not enough?

choices.text: A pre-check is only safe when it runs in the same HTTP handler as the insert
It is enough once an index exists on email, since indexes serialize writes
The SELECT has to be built with string concatenation to match the exact value
Two concurrent requests can both pass the pre-check before either one inserts

choices: A pre-check is only safe when it runs in the same HTTP handler as the insert
It is enough once an index exists on email, since indexes serialize writes
The SELECT has to be built with string concatenation to match the exact value
Two concurrent requests can both pass the pre-check before either one inserts

items.explanation: 'A uniqueness pre-check can race; the database constraint must enforce the rule.' Check-then-insert is a time-of-check/time-of-use gap. Only a database constraint enforces uniqueness.

items.prompt: PATCH /tasks/t1/complete is sent twice, an hour apart. What should the task's completion timestamp be after the second call?

choices.text: Unset, because a second completion toggles the task back to the open state
Unchanged only if the client resends the original timestamp in the body
The time of the first call, since every repeat completion keeps that timestamp
The time of the second call, since the latest completion always wins

choices: Unset, because a second completion toggles the task back to the open state
Unchanged only if the client resends the original timestamp in the body
The time of the first call, since every repeat completion keeps that timestamp
The time of the second call, since the latest completion always wins

items.explanation: U04-02: 'Repeated completion preserves its first timestamp.' The operation is idempotent with respect to the recorded time.

items.prompt: The alert evaluator already holds a Redis leadership lease. Why does it still take a per-organization transaction advisory lock?

choices.text: The lease can expire mid-evaluation and so two evaluators could overlap
The advisory lock replaces the UNIQUE(episode_id, step) constraint on pages
Redis leases cannot be released early, so the advisory lock is the release path
Advisory locks are what make the outbox send each page exactly once

choices: The lease can expire mid-evaluation and so two evaluators could overlap
The advisory lock replaces the UNIQUE(episode_id, step) constraint on pages
Redis leases cannot be released early, so the advisory lock is the release path
Advisory locks are what make the outbox send each page exactly once

items.explanation: ADR 0004: the lease 'reduces duplicate evaluator work' but 'The database transaction advisory lock serializes each organization even if a lease expires mid-work.' The lease is only rechecked between organizations.

items.prompt: Two bad POST /notes bodies arrive: `{"text": ` (truncated) and `{"text": 42}`. Where does each one fail in the worked example's pipeline?

choices.text: Field validation catches the truncated body, and the parser catches the 42
Both reach the domain logic, which rejects them while assigning the next ID
The truncated body fails parsing, and the number one fails field validation
Both fail JSON parsing, because neither contains a valid text string value

choices: Field validation catches the truncated body, and the parser catches the 42
Both reach the domain logic, which rejects them while assigning the next ID
The truncated body fails parsing, and the number one fails field validation
Both fail JSON parsing, because neither contains a valid text string value

items.explanation: 'Malformed JSON fails parsing; a well-formed invalid object fails field validation.' Parsing and validation are separate stages the guide asks you to trace separately.

items.prompt: An alert is firing when its metric stops reporting entirely for a while. What does the threshold rule do with the missing data?

choices.text: It treats the missing samples as low values and resolves the alert
It clears pending continuity but does not mark the firing alert recovered
It treats the missing samples as high values and escalates the page
It backfills the gap from the last observed sample and keeps evaluating it normally

choices: It treats the missing samples as low values and resolves the alert
It clears pending continuity but does not mark the firing alert recovered
It treats the missing samples as high values and escalates the page
It backfills the gap from the last observed sample and keeps evaluating it normally

items.explanation: 'Missing data clears pending continuity but does not assert recovery of a firing alert.' and 'no outage backfill is inferred.'

items.prompt: A client retries an ingest batch with the same idempotency key but serializes the JSON object keys in a different order. Per the review notes, what can happen?

choices.text: Nothing changes: the hash is computed over a canonical, key-sorted body
It gets 413, because re-serialization can push the body past the size limit
It always succeeds, because the hash ignores the body and uses only the key
It can get a 409, since the hash covers JSON.stringify of the parsed body

choices: Nothing changes: the hash is computed over a canonical, key-sorted body
It gets 413, because re-serialization can push the body past the size limit
It always succeeds, because the hash ignores the body and uses only the key
It can get a 409, since the hash covers JSON.stringify of the parsed body

items.explanation: The content hash is sha256(signal + JSON.stringify(request.body)); key-order changes can change the stringified form, so the note says retries must resend the same payload.

items.prompt: An ingest batch COMMITs but the response is lost; the client retries with the same idempotency key and identical content. What does the store do?

choices.text: It deletes the first batch and re-inserts the retry inside a whole new transaction
It inserts a second batch, since content-hash deduplication is off by default
It throws IdempotencyConflict, because any row with that request ID already exists
The conflicting INSERT returns no row, and since the hashes match it returns quietly

choices: It deletes the first batch and re-inserts the retry inside a whole new transaction
It inserts a second batch, since content-hash deduplication is off by default
It throws IdempotencyConflict, because any row with that request ID already exists
The conflicting INSERT returns no row, and since the hashes match it returns quietly

items.explanation: store.ts runs INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING; with no row returned it SELECTs payload_hash and only throws when the hash differs. Identical content returns quietly, so the retry resolves the duplicate.

items.prompt: An outbox worker sends a page, the provider accepts it, and the worker crashes before committing. What does ADR 0004 say about the result?

choices.text: The page moves straight to dead-letter status and is never retried
The UNIQUE(page_id, kind) constraint blocks the second HTTP request
The send can repeat, and only provider idempotency can suppress that duplicate
SKIP LOCKED guarantees the claimed page is never sent a second time

choices: The page moves straight to dead-letter status and is never retried
The UNIQUE(page_id, kind) constraint blocks the second HTTP request
The send can repeat, and only provider idempotency can suppress that duplicate
SKIP LOCKED guarantees the claimed page is never sent a second time

items.explanation: 'A crash after provider acceptance but before commit can repeat a send. Provider idempotency is required for duplicate suppression outside the database.'

items.prompt: A learner submits a working feature that an agent mostly wrote, and explains it fluently. How does the assessment guide treat that?

choices.text: As invalid work that must be deleted before any rating is given
As a challenge-out of the whole module, since the tests are green
As delivery evidence only, since fluent explanation is not proof of independent skill
As a rating of 3, since the task was completed, verified and explained

choices: As invalid work that must be deleted before any rating is given
As a challenge-out of the whole module, since the tests are green
As delivery evidence only, since fluent explanation is not proof of independent skill
As a rating of 3, since the task was completed, verified and explained

items.explanation: 'Fluent explanation alone is insufficient... A successful copied implementation is delivery evidence, not independent skill.' Fluent explanation does not change that.

items.prompt: Redis, which holds the per-key rate counters, goes down. How does an admitted, authenticated ingest request behave?

choices.text: It is allowed through, and counting resumes once Redis comes back online
It falls back to a per-process in-memory counter until Redis recovers
It fails closed with 503 and Retry-After instead of an in-memory fallback
It gets 429 with Retry-After: 60, the same response as an exceeded rate limit

choices: It is allowed through, and counting resumes once Redis comes back online
It falls back to a per-process in-memory counter until Redis recovers
It fails closed with 503 and Retry-After instead of an in-memory fallback
It gets 429 with Retry-After: 60, the same response as an exceeded rate limit

items.explanation: ADR 0002: 'no in-memory fallback on outage. Fail-closed Redis outage returns 503.' The limiter's catch in server.ts returns 503 with Retry-After: 2.

items.prompt: Your client calls POST /notes while the API process is down. What does the client observe, according to U04?

choices.text: A 503 Service Unavailable, always generated by Fastify's default error handler
A 500 Internal Server Error, because the server failed to handle the request
No HTTP response at all, since a refused connection has no status code
A 400 Bad Request, since nothing on the server could parse any of the body

choices: A 503 Service Unavailable, always generated by Fastify's default error handler
A 500 Internal Server Error, because the server failed to handle the request
No HTTP response at all, since a refused connection has no status code
A 400 Bad Request, since nothing on the server could parse any of the body

items.explanation: U04 stresses that 'A network failure differs from a 400 or 500 response' and 'A failed connection has no HTTP response status.' A status code only exists when a server actually answered.

items.prompt: In the U04-02 task API, a client sends a 20 KiB body to POST /tasks. Which response and store state does the acceptance require?

choices.text: 201, because the body limit only applies to PATCH /tasks/:id/complete
413, and a placeholder task is stored so the task ID sequence stays dense
413, and the memory store is left unchanged by the rejected creation
400, and the task is stored with its title truncated to fit the 16 KiB limit

choices: 201, because the body limit only applies to PATCH /tasks/:id/complete
413, and a placeholder task is stored so the task ID sequence stays dense
413, and the memory store is left unchanged by the rejected creation
400, and the task is stored with its title truncated to fit the 16 KiB limit

items.explanation: The task spec fixes '413 for bodies above 16 KiB' and the acceptance says 'Rejected creation leaves the store unchanged.'

items.prompt: Given `pages integer CHECK (pages > 0)` with no other constraint on pages, which INSERT succeeds?

choices.text: One with pages -5, because integer columns skip CHECK evaluation
One with pages NULL, since a CHECK by itself never rejects NULL
One with pages 0, because CHECK constraints only run on UPDATE statements
None that omit pages, because a CHECK constraint implies NOT NULL

choices: One with pages -5, because integer columns skip CHECK evaluation
One with pages NULL, since a CHECK by itself never rejects NULL
One with pages 0, because CHECK constraints only run on UPDATE statements
None that omit pages, because a CHECK constraint implies NOT NULL

items.explanation: 'The pages check rejects zero but permits NULL unless a separate NOT NULL constraint forbids it. Test the promise each constraint actually makes.' Only a separate NOT NULL would forbid the NULL row.
